## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured points (N≥4000) sit beyond the L1d spill at N≈963, so the curve starts in L2. At q=0.01, ns/p falls slightly from 8.85 (N=4000) to 8.146 (N=262000) as working set grows through the L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 — there is no knee, only a gentle decline from overhead amortization, then a mild rise to 8.758 at N=4M. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: the plateau moves from ~8.1–8.8 ns/p (q=0.01) to ~8.6–9.3 (q=0.05) to ~11.2–11.9 (q=0.25). Small-N overhead is pronounced at higher churn — N=4000 costs 12.684 ns/p at q=0.05 and 13.686 at q=0.25 — but flattens by N=16000 in every series.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.35 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01, which is 33% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algorithm is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: it never crosses into the streaming regime. Bandwidth is depressed at small N by per-particle overhead (7.68 GB/s at N=4000, q=0.01; 4.97 GB/s at N=4000, q=0.25), stabilizes by N=16000, then drifts down at N≥1M as death-rate-dependent respawn cost accumulates (7.85→7.76 GB/s from N=1M to 4M at q=0.01; 5.80→5.72 at q=0.25). The hypothesis predicts approaching the ceiling; the algorithm peaks at one-third of it.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized loop1 across the components of a single particle, not across particles. `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` and `mov.s v17[3], v6[0]` assemble four float components into one register, then `fmul.4s v6, v17, v3` and `fadd.4s v6, v7, v6` operate on all four lanes. A 2-lane path follows with `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s`. The `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x10]` is an indexed single-element load — a mini-gather into one lane. Loop2 is entirely scalar: `fcmp`/`fcvtzs`/`csel` chains for clamping, and 16 `strb` byte-granular stores with `csel` saturation to 0xff. The component-wise vec on stride-68 data explains the low bandwidth — each 68-byte particle yields only a handful of vector ops — and the loop2 scatter's byte stores cap it further.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algorithm peaks at 8.35 GB/s (33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=262000, and never approaches streaming. Component-wise autovec (`fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` on one particle's four floats) generates too little memory traffic per iteration to saturate bandwidth, and loop2's scalar `strb` scatter with `csel` clamping adds a branchy floor that rises with death rate (11.2 ns/p at q=0.25 vs 8.1 at q=0.01). The hypothesis fails even in the lowest-churn regime measured.
